topic: Applied Psychology Options (Child / Criminal / Environmental / Sport and Exercise)
subject: psychology

moments.title: Dimensions of Personality
moments.body: Eysenck uses factor analysis on military-hospital data to identify extraversion and neuroticism as core dimensions.

moments.title: Crime and Personality
moments.body: Eysenck argues criminality reflects high extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism with under-aroused nervous systems.
moments.takeaway: Biological trait theory reaches into forensic psychology.

moments.title: Mass retractions
moments.body: An institutional inquiry recommends retraction of 26 Eysenck papers; 14 are retracted by 2020.
moments.takeaway: Posthumous reckoning can rewrite a research legacy.

now.title: Big Five and beyond
now.body: The Five-Factor Model dominates modern personality research; biological correlates are weaker than once claimed.
now.open_questions: What is the appropriate balance of personality and situational explanation for offending?

reflection: Eysenck's career illustrates both the power and the risks of bold trait theorising.
